justification: Mechanism studied is the cross-session long-term memory write/retrieve path, with persistence strategies tailored to sliding-window and RAG memory; a new attack technique measured on lab agent setups, not deployed.
Contribution is a prompt-based confidence/uncertainty signal that gates whether the agent proceeds or asks the user, i.e. deferral to a human; evaluated in the lab on WebShop/ALFWorld variants.

Headline artefact is MAFBench, a unified measurement suite plus taxonomy for comparing multi-agent frameworks, an instrument rather than a loop mechanism; the controlled study runs in the lab under standardized pipelines.

STRIDE decides whether an agentic loop is warranted at all versus a single LLM call, scoring agentic suitability to cut unnecessary deployments; applied to 30 real SRE/compliance tasks with six months of expert use in practice.

The runtime allocates how many LLM calls a pipeline gets, gating mode switches on a quality floor with a standard/two-phase/sequential escalation ladder; evaluated in the lab against LangGraph and DSPy baselines.

Contribution routes subtasks to specialized third-party agents via skill discovery, a market decision rule and an inter-agent protocol, i.e. the arrangement itself; validated by 239 simulations and 240 lab LLM tasks.

The proposed BOLAA strategy orchestrates multiple labour agents through a controller that manages inter-agent communication; claims rest on lab simulations across decision-making and multi-step reasoning environments.
Object of study is what two asymmetric agents send each other, with communication strategies and an environment verifier varied; a lab game extended from Einstein Puzzles, no deployed setting.

Deliverable is a failure-mode assessment of agent loops under malfunction-amplification attacks across attack methods, surfaces and properties, plus a detection probe; all evaluations are lab experiments on implemented agents.
SCL's controller checks preconditions and authorizes execution before any tool call, a pre-execution gate on the action; evidence is 360 lab episodes against ReAct and LangChain baselines.

The paper names its distinguishing claim as the integrated monitoring system detecting abnormal behaviour from execution patterns and output consistency; evaluated on a prototype in a lab multi-agent workflow environment.
Focus contributes an agent-controlled compaction policy that consolidates learnings and prunes raw history; measured in the lab on five SWE-bench Lite instances.

Proposed architecture gates high-risk operations via run-time attestation and audit agents verifying intent against behaviour; the OPERA benchmark is designed but no results are reported, so it argues rather than validates.

The object is feedback quality in the revise-on-feedback loop: output-only human feedback produces failure-mode oscillation instead of convergence; shown in a lab Blender task with a diagnostic intervention.

TME contributes a task memory tree holding step state that is read back through prompt synthesis on the active node path; supported by lab case studies and comparative experiments on multi-step tasks.

CostCraft rewrites reusable skills from the agent's own cost-attributed traces between tasks; the claim rests on removing preserve and prune patch lanes on held-out SpreadsheetBench and SkillsBench tasks in the lab.

Contribution is a diagnostic framework: 22 intrinsic failure properties across six lifecycle layers and an entropy formalism for silent failure, a new way of looking at agent disorder rather than a loop mechanism.

The framework broadens exploration of a large solution space by running many agents in parallel under a shared leaderboard reward that selects among candidate solutions; evidence is one lab testbed on catalog matching.

EvoTrainer is an outer loop that co-evolves the policy and its training harness from rollout evidence and accumulates reusable skills; validated on math, competitive programming and repository-level SWE benchmarks.

Title-only record: a MAPE control loop drives continuous improvement of a deployed agent from usage data, an outer loop changing the agent between episodes, reported from industry practice in the EACL industry track.

Actions are confined to finite catalogs enforced at the tool-output interface with a Lean-checked stability certificate, a policy gate on what the loop may execute; tested on 282 attack graphs and paired telemetry in the lab.

AICL fixes the order of steps through structured planning, probe-driven monitoring and event-based orchestration; support is qualitative experiments with the CyberLoop reference implementation, not a deployed setting.

The contribution is the collective arrangement: per-agent MAPE-K loops plus decentralized gossip dissemination, computational trust between peers and federated adaptation; empirical comparison against multi-agent baselines.

An evolution module beside the BDI reasoning loop elicits new requirements from experience and synthesizes new goals and code, changing the agent itself; support is a prototype demonstration in a simulated environment.

Semantic Kinematics adds a PID/EKF inner loop that selects the next navigation step without calling the LLM, determining what the loop does next; measured on a Wikipedia navigation benchmark against CoT agents.
